### Legacy Plots

These polar charts used the legacy polar attributes (`r` and `t` on `scatter` traces, with `angularaxis`/`radialaxis` at the top level of the layout), which have been removed from plotly.js. With plotly.core, the same charts are drawn with the `scatterpolar` and `scatterpolargl` [trace types](polar-chart.html), as below.

### Polar Scatter Chart

The microphone pick-up patterns are polar curves of the form $|a + (1 - a)\cos\theta|$.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

mic_patterns <- c(
  Figure8 = 0,
  Cardioid = 0.5,
  Hypercardioid = 0.25,
  Subcardioid = 0.7,
  Supercardioid = 0.37
)
t <- seq(0, 360, by = 6)

fig <- go_figure()
for (nm in names(mic_patterns)) {
  a <- mic_patterns[[nm]]
  fig <- fig |>
    add_scatterpolar(
      r = round(abs(a + (1 - a) * cos(t * pi / 180)), 3),
      theta = t,
      mode = "lines",
      opacity = 0.5,
      name = nm
    )
}
fig <- fig |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Mic Patterns",
    polar = go_polar(angularaxis = go_polar_angularaxis(rotation = 90))
  )

fig
```

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

trials <- read.csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/hobbs-pearson-trials.csv"
)

fig <- go_figure()
for (i in 1:5) {
  fig <- fig |>
    add_scatterpolar(
      r = trials[[paste0("trial_", i, "_r")]],
      theta = trials[[paste0("trial_", i, "_theta")]],
      mode = "markers",
      opacity = 0.5,
      name = paste("Trial", i)
    )
}
fig <- fig |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Hobbs-Pearson Trials",
    polar = go_polar(bgcolor = "rgb(229, 229, 229)")
  )

fig
```

### Reference
See `go_scatterpolar()` and `go_polar()` for more information and chart attribute options!
